subject: Request: Eyrie onboarding — subprocessor compliance kit & proposed cutover windows
messages:
From: Elena Mora <elena.mora@eyriedata.com>
To: priyom_das@redwood.com
Cc: legal@eyriedata.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Request: subprocessor compliance kit & proposed cutover windows for Eyrie onboarding

Hi Priyom,

We're kicking off the onboarding for Eyrie DataBroker to consume Redwood inference APIs as part of our managed analytics pipeline. To satisfy our internal procurement and privacy review, can you please share:

- The current subprocessor roster that will touch Eyrie customer data (names, roles, geographic egress by processor) in a spreadsheet we can import.
- SOC 2 scope extract or report references covering processing systems used in production.
- KMS/HSM attestation or a short note on key management and where encryption keys are hosted.
- Any planned changes to subprocessors in the next 60 days and the intended cutover windows if applicable.

For planning purposes we're hoping to target a cutover window between Dec 10–15 but can be flexible if there are dependencies on your end. If you have a standard compliance pack (CSV + supporting PDFs) that would be ideal — otherwise a quick spreadsheet and a couple PDFs will do.

Can you also let me know who on your side is best for procurement/legal to coordinate doc signing and timing?

Thanks — appreciate the quick turnaround.

Best,
Elena Mora
Head of Vendor Risk & Procurement
Eyrie DataBroker
Attachments: none
From: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
To: Elena Mora <elena.mora@eyriedata.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 10:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: subprocessor compliance kit & proposed cutover windows for Eyrie onboarding

Hi Elena — thanks for the note and welcome.

We're happy to provide the materials. I've attached an initial subprocessor roster spreadsheet (redwood-subprocessor-roster-20261120.xlsx) that lists our current processors, the roles they perform (e.g., observability, CDN, persistent storage), and the primary egress regions. That file is intended to be importable.

Quick answers up front:
- SOC 2: we will attach a scoped extract (SOC2-Scope-Extract) capturing the infra & serving runtime used for inference — Kimberly is looping in legal to confirm the exact pages you need.
- KMS: we use a cloud KMS with optional HSM-backed keys for enterprise/private deployments; I'm attaching the KMS attestation stub Kimberly recommended.
- Planned changes: no planned subprocessor additions between now and Dec 15 in our hosted offering; we do have routine patching of CDN partners that are non-customer-facing. If anything changes we'll provide at least 30 days notice and an impact matrix.

Next steps I propose:
1) Kimberly — can you confirm the SOC2 pages and attach the attestation PDF?
2) Jordan — can you propose a tentative cutover runbook (metrics to watch, rollback criteria) for the Dec 10–15 window?
3) Elena — can you share your procurement contact so we can push the DPA for signature and confirm the DocuSign link?

I've attached: redwood-subprocessor-roster-20261120.xlsx (spreadsheet).

— Priyom
Lead, Platform Partnerships
Redwood Inference
Attachments: redwood-subprocessor-roster-20261120.xlsx (xlsx)
From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>
To: Elena Mora <elena.mora@eyriedata.com>, Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 13:27:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: subprocessor compliance kit & proposed cutover windows for Eyrie onboarding

Hi Elena / team — looping in Legal.

Attached are two items that should address most of your procurement/privacy checks: a short KMS attestation and a SOC 2 scope extract that highlights the systems in-scope for serving and observability. Please note the SOC 2 extract is a restricted excerpt; we can provide the full report under an NDA or via your vendor portal as required.

A couple of clarifications/questions from our side:
- Please confirm whether Eyrie needs the KMS keys to be rotatable by you (customer-controlled keys) or Redwoods-managed keys. For private deployments we can support customer-managed HSM-backed keys; hosted customers typically use Redwood-managed KMS with encrypted-at-rest keys.
- Does your internal policy require separate subprocessors to be listed by legal entity *and* by service name? We've included both columns in the attached roster but can expand.
- Procurement contact — if you can share an email we will send the current DPA for signature and a DocuSign link.

Jordan — once we confirm the key policy ask I can sign off on the DPA clauses; please add the operational runbook items Priyom requested.

Thanks,
Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Privacy & Security
Redwood Inference
Attachments: kms-attestation-20261120.pdf (pdf), soc2-scope-extract-20261120.pdf (pdf)
From: Elena Mora <elena.mora@eyriedata.com>
To: Priyom Das <priyom_das@redwood.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com>, Jordan Blake <jordan_blake@redwood.com>, procurement@eyriedata.com, legal@eyriedata.com
Date: Fri, 20 Nov 2026 16:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Request: subprocessor compliance kit & proposed cutover windows for Eyrie onboarding

Thanks — this is helpful and fast, much appreciated.

Procurement contact is procurement@eyriedata.com (Emily Li). We'll expect a DocuSign DPA link from your team. For keys: we prefer customer-managed keys for production traffic, but can pilot with Redwood-managed keys during initial onboarding if it's easier — we'd like a plan to move to customer-managed HSM within 90 days.

We're good to meet to walk through the roster and edit controls; here's a link to schedule a 30-min slot for next week: https://calendar.eyriedata.com/meet/priyom-redwood-review.

If you can send the DocuSign envelope, Emily will start the internal approval. Also: can you confirm you'll provide at least 30 days' notice for any subprocessor changes after we go live?

We'll aim to finalize the DPA and cutover plan by Dec 2 so we can execute the Dec 10–15 window.

Best,
Elena Mora
Head of Vendor Risk & Procurement
Eyrie DataBroker
